strings.name: François Pinault
strings.summary: Starting in the Breton timber trade, Pinault expanded through acquisitions into retail and luxury, founding the group that became Kering and the Artémis investment company. After gradually transferring management to his son, he concentrated on contemporary art and opened exhibition venues in Venice and Paris. His commercial influence intersects with the extension of a private collection into public cultural spaces.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded a commercial group and developed its luxury businesses while building an internationally influential art collection.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education

strings.highlights.h1.title: Business group
strings.highlights.h1.text: Built the group later known as Kering through distribution, retail and luxury-brand acquisitions.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Public art venues
strings.highlights.h2.text: Supported contemporary-art venues at Palazzo Grassi, Punta della Dogana and the Paris Bourse de Commerce.
